schools.title: Dental hygiene schools by state
schools.description: How many colleges in each state reported dental hygiene awards for 2023-24, with national totals by award level and type of college, from the US Department of Education.
schools.heading: Dental hygiene schools by state
intro: Dental hygiene programs are accredited by the Commission on Dental Accreditation (CODA). The typical entry requirement for the job is an associate's degree (US Bureau of Labor Statistics).

This page shows how many colleges reported dental hygiene awards to the US Department of Education for 2023-24, in the US and in each state. Choose your state to see its colleges, local pay and how to get licensed there.
details: These figures count colleges that reported dental hygiene awards. They are not a count of accredited programs. Before applying, check a program's accreditation with the Commission on Dental Accreditation (CODA) [CODA PROGRAM SEARCH, OFFICIAL LINK] and its approval with the state dental board.
sources: US Bureau of Labor Statistics, Occupational Outlook Handbook: Dental Hygienists (entry requirement)
[Commission on Dental Accreditation (CODA), program list, page and date checked]

licensing.title: Dental hygienist licensing by state
licensing.description: Every state requires dental hygienists to be licensed, and the requirements differ from state to state. The usual steps, and the rules in each state.
licensing.heading: Dental hygienist licensing by state
intro: Every state requires dental hygienists to be licensed, and the requirements differ from state to state (US Bureau of Labor Statistics).
The usual route has five steps. Each state's page explains the rules there.
sources: US Bureau of Labor Statistics, Occupational Outlook Handbook: Dental Hygienists (licensing)

boardExam.title: The dental hygiene national board exam (NBDHE)
boardExam.description: The national written exam for dental hygienists is the National Board Dental Hygiene Examination (NBDHE), run by the Joint Commission on National Dental Examinations (JCNDE).
boardExam.heading: The national board exam for dental hygienists
intro: The national written exam is the National Board Dental Hygiene Examination (NBDHE). It is run by the Joint Commission on National Dental Examinations (JCNDE).

Every state requires dental hygienists to be licensed, and the requirements differ from state to state (US Bureau of Labor Statistics). For the clinical exam and the other rules in your state, see your state's page.
